arms.label: Ember
evidence: Trace explicitly reports inspection finding six rather than five buttons and three USB-C-like rear sockets.
A targeted edit produced five buttons and distinct USB-C plus two micro-HDMI openings; original-detail inspection confirms both improvements.
The corrected final was visually inspected and is the sole image linked as final; archived hashes match the intermediate and corrected files.
Broad engineering risks are disclosed, but prose claims a recessed illuminated power button while the image and edit prompt show only five keys and an amber status light.

arms.label: Harbor
evidence: Trace shows generation and file handling but no view-image call or stated visual inspection.
No contradiction or correction is reported.
One final presentation image is delivered; its dimensions and archived SHA agree with the recorded artifact.
Prose, prompt, and image consistently show eight side-rail keys, a separate power control, four USB-A ports, Ethernet, one rear fan, and a rear connector bay.
The response clearly identifies the render as an appearance reference rather than verified CAD and discloses hardware, fit, thermal, acoustic, RF, and manufacturing uncertainties.

arms.label: Quartz
evidence: Trace contains generation, file relocation, metadata checking, and file enumeration, but no visual-inspection call or inspection statement.
No contradiction or correction is reported.
The sole final image matches the archived SHA and stated 1536×1024 dimensions.
Prompt, prose, and visible image agree on five keys, two front intake bands, four USB-A ports plus Ethernet, one rear exhaust, and USB-C plus two rear HDMI openings.
The response explicitly disclaims proven fit, thermal capacity, acoustics, strength, compliance, and manufacturability and lists unresolved assumptions.

arms.label: Willow
evidence: Trace includes an original-detail view-image call followed by a visual-check statement.

The agent noticed that the render contained eight controller keys plus a ninth power key and a full-size HDMI-shaped rear opening, contrary to the generation prompt's eight total keys and micro-HDMI opening.
It corrected the written specification by identifying the ninth key as power and the HDMI as a panel extension, improving prose-image agreement without correcting the image itself.
The final response explicitly discloses these reinterpretations and extensive remaining validation risks.
One final image is delivered and its SHA matches the archive, but the archived generation prompt still disagrees with the final image and prose on key count and HDMI form.

comparative_result: Ember performed the strongest image-quality-control loop: it inspected, identified concrete defects, regenerated, and visibly improved the result. Willow inspected and reconciled discrepancies in prose but did not repair the image, leaving mixed improvement and partial archive agreement. Harbor and Quartz delivered coherent single artifacts with good disclosure and agreement, but their traces contain no visual inspection or corrective loop.
disagreements: The main judgment ambiguity is Willow: its prose correction improves delivery consistency, but it rationalizes generated deviations instead of visually fixing them. Ember retains a smaller prose-image mismatch around the claimed illuminated power button. Harbor's rear HDMI scale is visually somewhat ambiguous, but not clear enough to mark artifact disagreement.
